newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Key long bonds recovered from weaker intraday levels to end steady after a slow day characterised by early position squaring as many players attended a South African golf day.
At 1400 GMT the key R150 stock was yielding 15.49 percent from 15.53 percent late on Thursday after weakening to around 15.56 percent during the morning.

Bond traders said the market had been in a correction phase after recent strong gains which saw government's benchmark R150 stock firm to a best 15.43 level level during the week, but the outlook remains positive.
Foreign demand for local bonds has fed a growing mood of optimism on both the bond and currency markets since the start of the year.
"After a strong run we're now looking at a correction before strength can set in again," a bond trader at a leading bank said.

Another said buyers had withdrawn a bit after the buoyant mood that swept the market at the start of the week. Players were focusing on the options close-out on February 6 and the market was likely to tread water between 15.40 to 15.60 percent in the lead-up to the event, the trader said.
South Africa's continued high money market of more than 10 billion rand a day was as niggling factor but traders were optimistic there would be eventual relief.
"We're not too worried...it's bound to come down," one said.
Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals told Reuters this week the liquidity squeeze helped the authorities keep bank credit extension in check and he was in no hurry to reduce the shortage.

Next week, the bond market will be taking its cue from key economic data. The December consumer price index as well as money supply and private sector growth figures are scheduled for release on Tuesday.

The consensus forecast of economists polled by Reuters was for a year-on-year inflation rate of 9.6 percent from 9.2 percent in November, and a month-on-month increase of 1.0 percent compared to 0.4 percent.

But analysts expect growth in the key monetary aggregates to come down, mainly as a result of the very high year-ago comparative base. The consensus forecast was for M3 year-on-year growth of 14.3 percent from 15.32 in November while private credit is seen expanding 16.3 percent against 17.10 percent.
Foreigners bought a net 39.11 million rands worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 80.67 million on Wednesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 42.28 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from Wednesday's 9.20 billion rand, it said.
The rand had an uneventful day, ending firmer on the dollar after a brief test below 4.61 during the morning.

It closed at 4.6130/6180 on the dollar from 4.6255/6305 at Thursday's close and a morning high bid of 4.6080 after an upbeat week which saw the local unit hitting new highs despite the dollar's strength against other currencies.
Forex traders said the rand was lifted by local exporter and offshore dollar sales on Friday but cautioned that there could be some profit-taking early next week.
"Offshore players have already bought quite a few rands so there could be some profit-taking," a senior trader said.
The longer-term outlook was bullish, Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank foreign exchange director Willie Potgieter told Reuters.

"I don't think the rand is going to appreciate by five or ten percent in value all of a sudden but at least the trend is much more of sideways trend and mayby choppy within a range other than just the depreciation trend that we saw last year," said Potgieter.
On the crosses, the rand was last at 0.3965/33971 on the mark from 0.3547/3553 on Thursday while against sterling it was at 7.5092/5219 from 7.5362/5453.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 10.233 billion rand on Thursday from 10.048 billion rand on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank said.

Leading banks quoted their three-month NCD rates slightly lower at between 17.20-17.40 percent from 17.25-17.40 percent while 90-day BA rates were also lower at 16.50-16.70 percent from 16.55-16.75 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
